html:
SMTO-EML-0011 — Your email is too large to send

GUID: c025d5b3-63d5-5db9-b7d1-5781d99ebbd9
Slug: email-attachment-too-large
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The email, including its attachments, is bigger than SMTO or your mail server allows. SMTO stopped before sending it, so nothing went out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Remove some attachments or replace them with smaller versions. All attachments together must stay under about 20 MB. SMTO refuses attachments that add up to more than about 20 MB.
  2. Share very large files another way, such as a link to shared storage, and mention it in the message instead. Your mail server may accept much less than 20 MB, and its own limit applies too.
  3. If someone set a lower maximum message size in the sender profile in Parameter Store, ask the person who manages SMTO whether it can be raised. It can't go above 25 MB. The sender profile sets the largest email SMTO will try to send through that account.
  4. Ask SMTO to send the smaller email. Nothing was sent, so sending the reduced email won't create a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting the attachment sizes. If the details mention a size mismatch rather than a limit, report it; shrinking the email won't fix that.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The email exceeded a size limit (attachments over 20 MiB in total, MIME over the profile's max_message_bytes or the server's advertised SIZE), or the actual MIME length differed from the declared message_bytes.

What this means

  • Attachments exceed their aggregate bound, MIME exceeds the profile/server SIZE allowance, or actual MIME length differs from declared message_bytes. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • Attachments exceed their aggregate bound, MIME exceeds the profile/server SIZE allowance, or actual MIME length differs from declared message_bytes.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare raw attachment bytes, final MIME bytes, metadata count and server SIZE separately.

How to fix it

  • Reduce attachments below the 20 MiB aggregate limit and keep the complete MIME within the profile's max_message_bytes (default and maximum 25 MiB) and the server's SIZE extension. If the error reports a mismatch between actual and declared message_bytes, treat it as a preparation defect and report it rather than trimming content.
  • Reduce oversized content deliberately or correct inconsistent size metadata; keep exact complete MIME within profile and server limits.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • Complete MIME fits all applicable limits and matches the exact declared byte count.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
